You're working in the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon-wt-games (a git worktree on branch feature/game-images-wizard-fixes — work directly in this tree, don't create a new worktree). Nxeon is a VPS/hosting platform (Next.js App Router). The owner asked for "move from hostinger to nxeon (and other providers) pages" — dedicated landing pages that target people currently on a competitor host who are searching to switch, e.g. "move from Hostinger to Nxeon" / "migrate from GoDaddy". This is DIFFERENT search intent from the existing `/vps-vs-hostinger`-style comparison pages (those target "X vs Y" comparison shoppers) — a migration page leads with "here's exactly how we move you over," personalized to the specific host they're leaving.

## What already exists (read these first, in this order)

1. `app/(marketing)/migrate/page.tsx` — the REAL, generic migration explainer. This describes an ACTUAL feature: Nxeon's worker SSHes into the customer's old server, scans it read-only, detects files/databases/Docker containers/apps, then migrates everything to the same paths with no downtime on the old server, for free. Read this file fully — its `STEPS` array and `FEATURES` array are the ONLY source of truth for what migration actually does. The real CTA is `/dashboard/migrate`.
2. `components/marketing/ComparePageLayout.tsx` — the shared layout every `vps-vs-X` page uses. Read it fully to understand the component library available (`Section`, `SectionTitle`, `Eyebrow`, `CtaBand`, `FeatureCard`, `Reveal`, `FaqJsonLd`, `AmbientField`, `ReviewBadges`, `PricingGrid`, `CompetitorLogo`, `CompareTable`/`ChooseGrid`, and the icon set in `components/marketing/icons`). You'll build a NEW shared layout, `components/marketing/MigrateFromPageLayout.tsx`, modeled on this one's structure/quality bar but migration-story-first instead of comparison-table-first.
3. Pick 2-3 of the existing `app/(marketing)/vps-vs-<provider>/page.tsx` pages (hostinger, godaddy, bluehost at least) and read them fully — they're thin data files (~80-90 lines) passing data into the shared layout. Your new provider pages should be the same shape: thin data files into your new shared layout.
4. `lib/vps-price-band.ts` — how the comparison pages pull live, real Nxeon pricing (`getVpsPriceBand`). Your pages must NOT hardcode any Nxeon price — pull it the same way.
5. `components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx` and how it's used/gated elsewhere — there was a real finding on this codebase (2026-08-12 readiness audit) that unlabeled demo review numbers (e.g. "Trustpilot 4.9/312") are misleading if not real. DO NOT invent testimonials, review scores, or customer quotes. If the existing layout you're modeling includes a testimonial slot, either reuse the exact same honest pattern the codebase already uses elsewhere (check how `ComparePageLayout`'s `CompareTestimonial` type is actually filled across existing vps-vs-X pages — read 2-3 to see if they use real/generic illustrative lines, not fake attributed quotes) or omit it entirely for these new pages. Never fabricate specific numbers, named people, or specific dollar savings you can't source.

## What to build

**A. `components/marketing/MigrateFromPageLayout.tsx`** — a new shared layout, props-driven (provider name, provider display name, a short honest list of 3-4 "reasons people leave <Provider>" bullets — general, defensible pain points like "shared-hosting-style VPS with less real root control", "confusing multi-tier upsell pricing", "limited Asia-Pacific presence" — ONLY include claims that are plausible/generic industry-knowledge, never invent a specific stat/incident about the named competitor). Section order should be something like:
   1. Hero: "Move from <Provider> to Nxeon" + one-line value prop + CTA to `/dashboard/migrate`
   2. The REAL 4-step migration story (reuse the actual STEPS content/meaning from `app/(marketing)/migrate/page.tsx` — don't invent new steps)
   3. "Why people move from <Provider>" — the 3-4 honest bullets (per-provider, passed as props)
   4. Real, DB-fed Nxeon plan pricing (reuse `getVpsPriceBand` / whatever `ComparePageLayout` uses for its live pricing section)
   5. FAQ (2-4 real, useful questions: "Will my site go down during the move?", "Do I need to give you my <Provider> password?", "What if something doesn't migrate cleanly?" — answer these from the REAL mechanics in migrate/page.tsx, not invented ones) + `FaqJsonLd`
   6. Closing `CtaBand` to `/dashboard/migrate`
   Include proper `Metadata` (title, description, canonical, openGraph, twitter) per page — SEO-important, model off how the vps-vs-X pages do their metadata.

**B. Ten page files**, one per provider, at `app/(marketing)/migrate-from-<slug>/page.tsx`:
   a2hosting, bluehost, cloudways, digitalocean, godaddy, hostgator, hostinger, ionos, kamatera, namecheap
   (these are the exact 10 that already have a matching `vps-vs-<slug>` comparison page — keep the slugs identical so the two families pair up). Each page is a thin data file: provider display name + the 3-4 honest "why people leave" bullets + metadata, passed into `MigrateFromPageLayout`. Use each provider's ACTUAL correct product name/branding (e.g. "Hostinger", "GoDaddy", "DigitalOcean", "A2 Hosting", "Cloudways", "Bluehost", "HostGator", "IONOS", "Kamatera", "Namecheap") — check the matching `vps-vs-<slug>/page.tsx` for the exact display name/capitalization they already use, for consistency.

**C. Cross-link the two families.** In each existing `app/(marketing)/vps-vs-<slug>/page.tsx`, add (or find if `ComparePageLayout` already has a slot for) a link to the matching `/migrate-from-<slug>` page near its migration section — something like "Already decided? See exactly how we move you over free →". Keep this a small, surgical addition, not a redesign of those pages.

**D. Add all 10 new routes to the sitemap** — find `app/sitemap.ts`, see how the existing `vps-vs-X` pages are listed, and add the new `migrate-from-X` routes the same way.

## Constraints

- Follow this codebase's existing conventions exactly (Tailwind classes, the `Section`/`Reveal`/icon patterns already in use) — don't introduce a new visual language.
- No fabricated stats, testimonials, review scores, or specific claims about a named competitor you can't source generically (e.g. never say "Hostinger's support takes 3 days" — that's inventing a fact). Stick to structural/product-model differences (shared hosting vs VPS focus, control-panel philosophy, regional footprint) which are safe, defensible category-level claims.
- Real Nxeon pricing only, pulled live — never hardcode a dollar figure.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` from /opt/nxeon-wt-games when done and fix any type errors before finishing.
- Do NOT run `git add`/`git commit` — just leave the files in the working tree. Do NOT touch node_modules or run a build.
- Do NOT modify any file outside `app/(marketing)/migrate-from-*/`, the new `components/marketing/MigrateFromPageLayout.tsx`, the 10 existing `vps-vs-*` pages (small cross-link addition only), and `app/sitemap.ts`.

When done, report: which 10 provider slugs you created, whether tsc passed clean, and a 1-sentence summary of what MigrateFromPageLayout's props shape looks like.
